metas.name: Anvil! The Story of Anvil
metas.description:
Artistic persistence continues here with no payoff in sight. Toronto's own Anvil: fifty-something metal pioneers who nearly made it in 1982, now delivering school lunches and playing to five people in Prague, still completely serious about the band.

Since 1978, Anvil has become one of heavy metal's most influential yet commercially unsuccessful acts. In 2006, after a fledging European tour Anvil sets out to record their thirteenth album and continue to follow their dreams.

metas.name: Dont Look Back
metas.description:
Pennebaker films celebrity as combat sport, at the moment it was invented. Inside Dylan's 1965 England tour: the cue-card sequence, Dylan dismantling journalists in hotel rooms, a persona manufactured in front of the lens.

Documentary covering Bob Dylan's 1965 tour of England, which includes appearances by Joan Baez and Donovan.

metas.name: Won't You Be My Neighbor?
metas.description:
Fred Rogers deploys gentleness as a discipline, not a temperament. He turns out to have been exactly as radical as he appeared: using children's television to insist, slowly and on purpose, that every child is lovable as they are.

An exploration of the life, lessons, and legacy of iconic children's television host Fred Rogers.

metas.name: Roadrunner: A Film About Anthony Bourdain
metas.description:
Charisma is both the gift and the mechanism of self-destruction in this film. Anthony Bourdain's rise and suicide, told by the friends and crew who travelled with him and remain angry and bewildered in roughly equal measure.

A documentary about Anthony Bourdain and his career as a chef, writer and host, revered and renowned for his authentic approach to food, culture and travel.

metas.name: Diego Maradona
metas.description:
Kapadia builds fame as a hostage situation where the hostage keeps scoring goals. Maradona's Naples years, assembled entirely from archive: adored as a god, pulled into the Camorra's orbit, collapsing under a worship no person could survive.

Constructed from over 500 hours of never-before-seen footage, this documentary centers on the career of celebrated football player Diego Maradona, who played for S.S.C. Napoli in the 1980s.

metas.name: Tim's Vermeer
metas.description:
Obsession becomes method here: an engineering argument settled by actually doing the thing. Inventor Tim Jenison, who can't paint, spends years testing his theory that Vermeer used optical devices — by building the device and painting a Vermeer with it.

Inventor Tim Jenison seeks to understand the painting techniques used by Dutch Master Johannes Vermeer.

metas.name: Tower
metas.description:
People inside an event remember it here as they actually lived it — partial, sensory, nothing like the news summary. The 1966 UT Austin sniper massacre retold in rotoscoped animation from survivors' memories, switching to real footage only at the end.

Animation, testimony, and archival footage combine to relate the events of August 1, 1966 when a gunman opened fire from the University of Texas clock tower, killing 16 people.

metas.name: Sherman's March
metas.description:
Out of failure, McElwee invents the personal documentary. He sets out to film Sherman's Civil War campaign, gets dumped before shooting starts, and the film becomes his disastrous search for love among old flames, narrated in a deadpan spiral.

Documentary filmmaker Ross McElwee sets out to make a movie about Union General Sherman's March to the Sea towards the end of the American Civil War, but keeps getting sidetracked by his own love life.

metas.name: Tarnation
metas.description:
For Caouette, self-documentation is a survival strategy. He assembles his life from family photos, answering-machine tapes and home video — a mother destroyed by shock treatments and lithium, a childhood spent performing for cameras — edited on iMovie for a few hundred dollars.

Filmmaker Jonathan Caouette's documentary on growing up with his schizophrenic mother -- a mixture of snapshots, Super-8 film, answering machine messages, video diaries, early short films, and more - culled from nineteen years of ...

metas.name: Ex Libris: The New York Public Library
metas.description:
A civic institution actually functions here as the thing it claims to be, which turns out to be quietly riveting. Wiseman, three hours, no narration: board meetings, story time, job-search classes, a branch deciding its budget at the New York Public Library.

A look within the walls of the New York Public Library.

metas.name: Primary
metas.description:
Politics and television fuse in this film, visible as it happens. The film that invented American cinéma vérité: newly portable sync-sound cameras follow Kennedy and Humphrey through the 1960 Wisconsin primary, into rooms no camera had entered before.

Cinéma vérité feature that follows presidential hopefuls John F. Kennedy and Hubert H. Humphrey during the 1960 Wisconsin primary.

metas.name: Best Boy
metas.description:
Love is expressed here as letting go, at the lowest possible volume. Philly, a developmentally disabled man in his fifties whose elderly parents have done everything for him, is gently taught to live more independently — because they won't always be there.

In this documentary, the director follows the day-to-day activities of his intellectually disabled, middle-aged cousin Philly over a three-year period.

metas.name: The Cruise
metas.description:
Timothy 'Speed' Levitch turns a minimum-wage job into a total worldview. A New York double-decker tour guide, he treats the job as performance philosophy, riffing on grid plans, pigeons and mortality to busloads of tourists.

Timothy "Speed" Levitch, an eccentric New York City tour bus guide, takes tourists around the island of Manhattan and shares an archive of beautifully distorted information about the city.

metas.name: Häxan
metas.description:
A lecture dissolves into delirium in Christensen's silent Swedish study of witchcraft, which keeps abandoning its own format for re-enactments — sabbaths, torture chambers, possessed nuns — and from 1922 remains wilder than most folk horror made since.

Fictionalized documentary showing the evolution of witchcraft, from its pagan roots to its confusion with hysteria in Eastern Europe.

metas.name: This Is Not a Film
metas.description:
A banned director stages, in his living room, the film he is forbidden to make, marking out sets with tape on the carpet. Smuggled out of Iran on a USB stick hidden in a cake; the title is the legal defence and the joke.

It's been months since Jafar Panahi, stuck in jail, has been awaiting a verdict by the appeals court. By depicting a day in his life, Panahi and Mojtaba Mirtahmasb try to portray the deprivations looming in contemporary Iranian ci...

metas.name: West of the Tracks
metas.description: An industrial civilisation is ending in real time. Nine hours inside Shenyang's collapsing factory district: workers showering in the plant, waiting for wages that aren't coming, singing karaoke as the furnaces cool. Shot alone on a DV camera; the scale is the argument.

metas.name: Land of Silence and Darkness
metas.description:
Communication is reduced to its minimum viable bandwidth. Fini Straubinger, deaf and blind, guides Herzog through a community touching hands to speak; one man was found at 30 having never learned any language at all.

Through examining Fini Straubinger, an old woman who has been deaf and blind since adolescence, and her work on behalf of other deaf and blind people, this film shows how the deaf and blind struggle to understand and accept a worl...

metas.name: Streetwise
metas.description:
Kids are left to raise themselves in public. Seattle street teenagers — panhandling, hustling, checking on each other — filmed with a patience that never once turns them into a lesson. The girl called Tiny will stay with you.

Gritty documentary that looks at the lives of teenagers living on the streets of Seattle.

metas.name: Hale County This Morning, This Evening
metas.description:
A place emerges through accumulated glances instead of a story. Alabama's Black Belt in fragments — a toddler's run down a hallway, a basketball game, a solar eclipse — edited like memory actually works.

A kaleidoscopic and humanistic view of the Black community in Hale County, Alabama.

metas.name: De Humani Corporis Fabrica
metas.description:
The body becomes an unexplored continent. Surgical cameras inside eyes, arteries and skulls in Paris hospitals — from the Leviathan team; medicine becomes pure landscape, and the doctors' small talk becomes the soundtrack.

An extraordinary adventure through the interior of the human body; or the discovery of an alien landscape of unprecedented beauty.

metas.name: Darwin's Nightmare
metas.description:
Globalisation takes the form of a food chain with guns in it. Nile perch flown from Lake Victoria to European tables while the same planes fly weapons in and Mwanza's people get the fish heads. Every interview makes it worse, quietly.

A documentary on the effect of fishing the Nile perch in Tanzania's Lake Victoria. The predatory fish, which has wiped out the native species, is sold in European supermarkets, while starving Tanzanian families have to make do wit...

metas.name: Our Daily Bread
metas.description:
Industrial food is shown with the commentary removed. No narration, no music: chick sorters, pig lines, salt mines, combine harvesters at night — just the sounds of the machinery and your own reaction, unassisted.

OUR DAILY BREAD is a wide-screen tableau of a feast which isn't always easy to digest - and in which we all take part. A pure, meticulous and high-end film experience that enables the audience to form their own ideas.

metas.name: 56 Up
metas.description:
Time itself becomes the special effect. The same British children filmed every seven years from 1964, now 56: the class predictions of the first episode meeting five decades of actual lives. You can feel the series itself ageing.

Director Michael Apted revisits the same group of British-born adults after a seven-year wait. The subjects are interviewed as to the changes that have occurred in their lives during the last seven years.

metas.name: Workingman's Death
metas.description:
This is labour that the modern world pretends is gone. Sulfur miners carrying loads up an Indonesian volcano, Nigerian slaughterhouse butchers, Pakistani shipbreakers — five portraits, no commentary, bodies doing what machines supposedly replaced.

A documentary on the extremes to which workers will go to earn a living.

metas.name: Taming the Garden
metas.description:
Wealth moves a landscape by sheer force. Georgia's richest man buys century-old trees from coastal villages and has them dug up, trucked and ferried upright across the sea to his private garden. No commentary; the image of a tree sailing is the whole argument.

Documentary follows trees that are transported, at great expense and inconvenience, from the coast of the Republic of Georgia to the private garden of that country's former prime minister.

metas.name: The Earth Is Blue as an Orange
metas.description:
Inside a real war, a family directs its own war movie. In the Donbas front-line town of Krasnohorivka, a mother and her kids shoot a fiction film about their lives between shelling — the camera as the household's way of staying sane, years before 2022 made the footage prophetic.

To cope with the daily trauma of living in a war-zone, Anna and her children are making a film together about their life in the most surreal surroundings.

metas.name: In the Basement
metas.description:
The film goes looking for what Austrians keep under the house. A documentary of suburban basements — Nazi memorabilia shrines, shooting ranges, doll collections, dungeons — each owner proudly giving the tour, each room arranged like a still life.

A documentary that reveals what its subjects do in their respective basements.

metas.name: Lightning Over Water
metas.description:
Two directors film a death; one of them is the dying man. Ray, terminal with cancer, co-directs his own ending — rehearsals, hospital corridors, arguments about whether the camera should be there at all. The complicit-camera question, asked by the subject himself.

Director 'Nicholas Ray' is eager to complete a final film before his imminent death from cancer. Wim Wenders is working on his own film Hammett (1983) in Hollywood, but flies to New York to help Ray realize his final wish. Ray's original intent is to make a fiction film about a dying painter who sails to China to find a cure for his disease. He and Wenders discuss this idea, but it is obviously unrealistic given Ray's state of health.

metas.name: Oxhide
metas.description:
A family lives inside 50 square metres and one failing business. The director films her own parents in their Beijing apartment and leather shop, in nine static shots, playing a version of herself; the bag shop is dying and everyone discusses dinner instead.

Director Liu Jiayin casts her parents and herself as fictionalized members of a Beijing family that has fallen on hard times and ekes out an existence by making bags out of oxhide for sale.

metas.name: Gates of Heaven
metas.description:
Two pet cemeteries — one failed, one thriving — and the people who can explain everything except themselves. Morris points the camera, asks almost nothing, and owners, renderers and salesmen deliver monologues that keep slipping from pets into the meaning of a life. His first film; it made Herzog eat a shoe.

A documentary about a pet cemetery in California, and the people who have pets buried there.

metas.name: Fast, Cheap & Out of Control
metas.description:
Four obsessions rhyme: a lion tamer, a topiary gardener, a mole-rat scientist and a robot engineer, intercut until their separate monologues start answering each other. The meaning emerges from the cuts themselves.

An exploration of the careers of four unrelated professionals: a lion tamer, a robotics expert, a topiary gardener, and a naked mole rat specialist.

metas.name: Between the Folds
metas.description:
Origami is followed where it stops being a craft: physicists folding proteins and deployable space lenses, a man who folds a single sheet into a full orchestra, theorems proved with creases. Ten paper artists and scientists, one shared conviction that a fold is a way of thinking.

Depicts a cast of fine artists and eccentric scientists (from MIT and NASA) who have devoted their lives to the unlikely medium of modern origami. Through their determination to reinterpret the world in paper, they arouse a fascin...

metas.name: A Glitch in the Matrix
metas.description:
Simulation theory is treated as a belief system with adherents, not a thought experiment. Speakers testify through digital avatars — itself the film's best argument — while clips and Philip K. Dick's 1977 "I am speaking to you from a replica" speech do the rest.

Documentary filmmaker Rodney Ascher tackles the question "are we living in a simulation?" with testimony, philosophical evidence and scientific explanation in his quest for the answer.

metas.name: The Mole Agent
metas.description:
An 83-year-old widower is hired to infiltrate a nursing home as a spy, and keeps forgetting to spy because the residents need a friend. A detective kit, a private investigator, hidden-camera glasses — all of it slowly repurposed into an undercover operation against loneliness.

A private investigator in Chile hires someone to work as a mole at a retirement home where a client of his suspects the caretakers of elder abuse.

metas.name: Images of the World and the Inscription of War
metas.description:
The gap between what an image records and what anyone sees in it is the whole subject. Allied reconnaissance planes photographed Auschwitz in 1944 while aiming at a factory next door; the camps sat in the archive, photographed in full and entirely unnoticed, for three decades. Farocki builds the film from that one distinction, stated in evidence.

Farocki’s intriguing and troubling film explores the processes of visual perception and how they affect our understanding of history and society. In a work reminiscent of the writings of Paul Virilio and Michel Foucault, Farocki examines a range of phenomena including aerial reconnaissance photos of the Auschwitz concentration camp.

metas.name: Five Dedicated to Ozu
metas.description:
The world is watched with the story removed. Five long static shots of the Caspian shore: waves, ducks, driftwood, a dog, the moon on water. No characters, no plot — just duration and attention, dedicated to the director who taught him both. A pure test of whether framing alone is enough.

Five sequences : 1) A piece of driftwood on the seashore, carried about by the waves 2) People walking on the seashore. The oldest ones stop by, look at the sea, then go away 3) Blurry shapes on a winter beach. A herd of dogs. A l...

metas.name: The Seasons
metas.description:
An Armenian mountain year unfolds as pure rhythm. Shepherds swept downriver clutching sheep, hay sleds flying downhill, a wedding, a flock pouring over a ridge — Pelechian's "distance montage" builds meaning between shots that never touch. Thirty minutes, no dialogue, elemental.

Film-essay about shepherds living in the Armenian highlands, about the contradiction and the harmony between man and nature.

metas.name: Histoire(s) du cinéma
metas.description: One man spends a decade re-editing the entire century of cinema inside his own head. Eight parts of layered clips, paintings, text and whispered commentary: film history as an apparatus that showed everything and recognised almost nothing, assembled as a kind of autobiography. A monument; take it in parts, the way it was made.

metas.name: The Missing Picture
metas.description:
A genocide whose footage doesn't exist is rebuilt in clay. Panh's family died under the Khmer Rouge; the propaganda reels show smiling peasants, so he carves little clay figures and dioramas to stand where the record is missing. The archive that exists, set against the reality that went unrecorded — and it is a documentary.

Rithy Panh uses clay figures, archival footage, and his narration to recreate the atrocities Cambodia's Khmer Rouge committed between 1975 and 1979.

metas.name: Mysterious Object at Noon
metas.description:
A story gets built by being handed from stranger to stranger across Thailand: a teacher, a boxer, market sellers each continue a tale about a boy and a mysterious object, and Apichatpong films their additions as fact. Storytelling as a chain of tellers, each adding loss and invention — a parlour game played across a country in 16mm black and white.

A camera crew travels through Thailand asking villagers to invent the next chapter of an ever-growing story.

metas.name: Pina
metas.description:
Dance becomes a language for things speech handles badly. Pina Bausch's company performs her pieces — in a theatre, on a traffic island, in a quarry, beside a tram line — shortly after her sudden death, the dancers' faces held in close-up between numbers. Shot in 3D that for once serves the subject: bodies occupying real space, at full scale.

A tribute to the late German choreographer Pina Bausch, as her dancers perform her most famous creations.

metas.name: The Truffle Hunters
metas.description:
A vanishing craft economy is seen from inside its last practitioners. Elderly men and their beloved dogs slip into Piedmont forests at night for white truffles worth more than gold, while dealers in suits wait at the edge of the woods. Shot like a Renaissance painting, scored by the men's own singing — competence, secrecy and interspecies partnership, all quietly ending.

Deep in the forests of Piedmont, Italy, a handful of men, seventy or eighty years old, hunt for the rare and expensive white Alba truffle-which to date has resisted all of modern science's efforts at cultivation.

metas.name: Infinite Football
metas.description:
One man has spent thirty years redesigning football. After an injury ended his career, Laurențiu Ginghină concluded the rules themselves were at fault — too much running, too many collisions — and has been revising them ever since, explaining octagonal pitches to indulgent officials. A deadpan documentary about systems-thinking as a life's consolation: the local instance of a universal type.

They talk about the beautiful game, but for Laurentiu Ginghina, it's not enough. Football must be modified, streamlined, freed from restraints; corners are to be rounded off, players assigned to zones and subteams, norms revised. ...

metas.name: HyperNormalisation
metas.description:
A world is governed by a story nobody believes anymore. Adam Curtis's essay film: after the 1970s, politicians, financiers and then tech platforms built a simplified, manageable fake version of reality — and eventually everyone, including its builders, lost the ability to act outside it. Syria, Putin, Trump, Brexit and the algorithm feed as symptoms of one condition: hypernormalisation, where the fake is known to be fake and continues anyway.

Adam Curtis explains how, at a time of confusing and inexplicable world events, politicians and the people they represent have retreated in to a damaging over-simplified version of what is happening.
